references.text: Moses recounts how the people asked to send spies to explore the land and its cities, paralleling the mission in Numbers 13:19 to assess the quality of the land and the fortifications of the cities.
Describes fortified cities with high walls, gates, and bars, linking to the question of whether the cities are in camps or fortresses.
The spies' report about the land flowing with milk and honey, yet containing fortified cities, is the direct answer to the questions asked in verse 19.
The people's fear of the great and fortified cities reported by the spies relates directly to the investigation of the cities' defenses.
Joshua sends spies to explore the land, especially Jericho, as a continuation of the same type of reconnaissance ordered in Numbers 13.
Caleb mentions the large fortified cities that the spies saw, referring back to the assessment of the cities' defensive strength.
